topic: Natural Language Processing: Transformers, Attention, and Tokenization

questions.scenario: A healthcare enterprise deploys a clinical decision-support pipeline utilizing a standard Transformer model with a WordPiece tokenizer trained primarily on Wikipedia and BookCorpus. When ingesting electronic health records (EHRs), complex pharmacological entities such as 'dextroamphetamine-amphetamine' and 'hydrochlorothiazide' are fragmented into 6 to 9 generic subword tokens. This causes sequence length explosions that frequently breach the 512-token ceiling and severely degrades named entity recognition (NER) macro F1-scores. The team must remediate this under strict edge-compute constraints without retraining the foundation model weights from scratch.
questions.question: Which vocabulary adaptation strategy is theoretically and practically optimal to prevent token inflation while preserving pre-trained contextual representations?
options: A) Retrain a Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer exclusively on clinical EHRs and re-initialize all Transformer positional and token embeddings using Xavier normal initialization.

B) Expand the existing WordPiece vocabulary with domain-specific clinical terms, initialize their new embedding vectors via the mean of their constituent subwords, and fine-tune only the embedding layer and task head.
C) Switch to UTF-8 byte-level tokenization without vocabulary expansion to ensure zero out-of-vocabulary instances, while freezing the encoder backbone.
D) Apply dynamic subword regularization during inference to randomly merge split tokens before passing them into the multi-head self-attention block.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Expand the existing WordPiece vocabulary with domain-specific clinical terms, initialize their new embedding vectors via the mean of their constituent subwords, and fine-tune only the embedding layer and task head.
questions.explanation: Over-fragmentation occurs when out-of-domain words are decomposed into excessive subwords, inflating sequence lengths and dispersing semantic mass. Retraining from scratch (Option A) discards general linguistic priors and requires vast compute. Byte-level tokenization (Option C) worsens sequence inflation. Subword regularization (Option D) is a training-time data augmentation method, not an inference-time reduction technique. Expanding the vocabulary, warm-starting new token embeddings with the mean of their subword embeddings, and fine-tuning preserves pre-trained weights while directly shrinking sequence length for domain terms.

questions.scenario: A legal-tech platform processes multi-party service contracts averaging 16,000 tokens per document. Using a standard multi-head self-attention architecture (Vaswani et al.), inferencing triggers CUDA Out-Of-Memory (OOM) faults on an Nvidia A100 (40GB) GPU at a batch size of 1. Profiling reveals that the intermediate attention map computation (softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k))) consumes over 32 GB of activation memory.
questions.question: Which attention mechanism variation provides an O(N) or O(N log N) asymptotic memory complexity while preserving both local lexical parsing and long-range cross-clause reference tracking?
options: A) Pure Sliding Window Attention with a fixed receptive field of k=512 tokens across all layers.
B) Sparse Attention combining local sliding window patterns with dedicated global attention tokens at structural boundaries.
C) Low-rank matrix factorization approximating the full N x N attention matrix using truncated Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) at each layer.
D) Replacing multi-head attention with Multi-Query Attention (MQA) while retaining the standard dense N x N dot-product computation.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Sparse Attention combining local sliding window patterns with dedicated global attention tokens at structural boundaries.
questions.explanation: Standard self-attention scales quadratically (O(N^2)) in both time and activation memory. Pure sliding window attention (Option A) reduces complexity to O(N * k), but loses direct long-range dependencies across distant contract clauses. Multi-Query Attention (Option D) reduces KV-cache memory during autoregressive generation but does not alter the O(N^2) activation cost of the attention matrix during parallel forward passes. Sparse Attention mechanisms (such as Longformer or BigBird) combine local sliding window attention with selected global tokens (e.g., at section headings or [CLS] tokens), cutting spatial complexity to O(N) while maintaining long-range cross-clause paths.

questions.scenario: An AI research group is pre-training an experimental deep Transformer encoder with high-dimensional attention projections where the per-head dimension d_k is scaled up to 512. During the initial training steps, gradients propagating through the self-attention layer vanish almost completely, and the attention distribution matrix collapses into near one-hot categorical vectors (peaked attention on single tokens). An engineer discovers that the implementation omitted the scaling factor in the dot-product attention formulation: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T)V.
questions.question: What is the exact mathematical mechanism causing gradient vanishing in this unscaled formulation?
options: A) As d_k grows large, the dot products grow large in magnitude, driving the softmax function into regions with near-zero gradients.
B) The unscaled dot product violates the unitary projection constraint, forcing the eigenvalues of QK^T to decay exponentially.
C) The absence of 1/sqrt(d_k) causes the spectral norm of the Value matrix V to explode, saturating the LayerNorm operations that follow.
D) The dot product variance collapses toward zero as d_k increases, causing numerical underflow in the numerator of the softmax function.
questions.correct_answer_text: A) As d_k grows large, the dot products grow large in magnitude, driving the softmax function into regions with near-zero gradients.
questions.explanation: Assuming components of Q and K are independent random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, their dot product has mean 0 and variance d_k. For large values of d_k (such as 512), the dot products attain large absolute magnitudes. Feeding large values into the softmax function pushes it into extreme saturation regions where the derivative of softmax (S_i * (delta_ij - S_j)) approaches zero. Scaling by 1/sqrt(d_k) pulls the variance back to 1, maintaining healthy gradient propagation during backpropagation.
